trust_decision.summary: The project trusts that a stored book slug, note slug or username is a single path component; the migrate exporters build output paths straight from those stored values (backend/cli/migrate.go:187,191,287,301,325) and the only ingress guard is huma's unanchored `pattern` tag (backend/db/types.go:26,41,70,77,10), which any value merely containing [a-z0-9-] satisfies, so '..%2F'-style slugs are stored and later joined into the export directory.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'book/note slug in migrate export'; the first path component assembled from stored data in the default export command is bookDir := path.Join(exportDir, user.Username, book.Slug) at :187, with noteDir at :191 and the asset join at :229 in the same loop.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the schema site and the CLI/IdP producers are trusted, non-HTTP input (signup/API bodies are where the report points) and that anchoring a huma tag cannot affect rows already saved in the database.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Export must round-trip: `migrate import` rebuilds book and note slugs verbatim from directory and file names, so an over-broad fix that rewrites/sanitises a component, or aborts the export on a bad row, silently renames or drops legitimate data - including legacy slugs such as 'a.b' that the unanchored pattern accepted before this fix.

O6_input_shapes: book slug in the create body (POST /api/books)
book slug in the update body (PUT /api/books/{bookID})
note slug in the create body (POST /api/books/{bookID}/notes)
note slug in the update body (PUT /api/notes/{noteID})
traversal at the start vs embedded in the value ('../../x' vs 'a/b' vs 'a.b'): only the anchored '^...$' form rejects the embedded and dotted shapes
stored component at the sink (rows already in the DB), for both the default exporter and the v1 exporter

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OIDC auto-provisioning: POST /api/auth/oidc-exchange creates a User whose Username is the ID token's preferred_username claim, without ever passing through CreateUser, so that value becomes the first path component of the export path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Optional OIDC deployment and a username supplied by a trusted identity provider, not by the API caller.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: handlers -> services, 2 packages / 2 files from the landing point; reachable whenever OIDC is configured (ENABLE_USER_CREATION defaults true)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `note-mark user add -u <username>` writes a User straight through db.DB.Create; the `pattern` tag is inert outside huma, so '-u ..' or '-u ../../tmp/x' is stored and later joined into the export path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin/operator-supplied CLI argument, not an external attacker path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file (1 file from the landing point)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `migrate import` creates books and notes whose slugs are taken verbatim from directory and file names with no slug validation; a note file named '...md' yields the slug '..', which the fix's filepath.Base(slug) != slug guard does not reject (Base("..") == ".."), so the exported note directory still escapes the book directory.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Import input is operator-provided and comes from the filesystem, where names cannot contain separators, so it looks safe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, import command (about 60 lines above the v1 export sink)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third exporter (e.g. a zip/tar or JSON-per-user dump) that repeats path.Join(exportDir, username, bookSlug, noteSlug).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already ships two exporters that differ only in layout (default and v1), so a maintainer adding another format would copy the existing loop and its joins verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Treating the already-present validate:"slug" tag (also at models.go:90) or a new gorm/DB-level check as the validation, and adding nothing at runtime.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: go-playground validator is wired only for AppConfig (backend/config/utils.go:23) and gorm ignores validate tags, so the tag reads like an enforced schema while doing nothing - a maintainer could plausibly extend that pattern instead of fixing the huma tags.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A user-lifecycle CLI command that writes a file per username (export/prune/backup) straight from the unvalidated users table.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: user.go already reads and writes users by raw username with no validation, so per-user file output there would inherit the same unvalidated path component.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22) through improper input validation (CWE-20) of a stored slug/username used as a filesystem path component

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0; module github.com/enchant97/note-mark/backend; `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` from backend/ (Dockerfile at backend/Dockerfile)
O10_build.project_tests: backend/storage/storage_test.go only (disk path helpers, :9-31); no tests for migrate import/export or for request-body validation at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add filepath.Base() to bookDir/noteDir in `migrate export` by copying the asset-name guard at migrate.go:223, verify by exporting one traversal slug, and stop - leaving the unanchored pattern tags, the username component and every non-HTTP producer untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Sibling GHSA-g49p-4qxj-88v3 (asset names) is already fixed at this commit (handler rejects separators at backend/handlers/assets.go:89-92; export applies a Base() check at backend/cli/migrate.go:223-228); that guard still admits an asset literally named '..', but asset names belong to the sibling advisory, so it was not pursued.
